description:
FILED s473t5c (#1501 round 4, `comp/` CHECK 1).  PRE-EXISTING.

perl still accepts `'` as a package separator (deprecated, warned under
`syntax`/`deprecated`, removal announced for a later release; perl 5.40.3
accepts it and t/comp/package.t exercises it under
`no warnings qw(syntax deprecated)`).  `$main'a` is `$main::a` and `$'b` is
`$main::b` -- note the SECOND form: a LEADING `'` means the CURRENT package,
and `$'` is also the punctuation variable POSTMATCH, so the discrimination is
"a `'` followed by an identifier character".

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):

    no warnings qw(syntax deprecated);
    $main::b = 42;
    $main'a = $'b;
    print "a=[$main::a] b=[$main::b]\n";
    $Foo'x = 7;
    print "Foo::x=[$Foo::x]\n";

    perl:  a=[42] b=[42]      Foo::x=[7]
    PCL :  Unhandled unbound-variable ... The variable |$'b| is unbound.

So the name is carried through to the CL symbol verbatim, pipe-quoted, and the
read dies.  A WRITE (`$main'a = …`) does not die -- it declares and writes a
global whose name contains a quote -- so the two spellings disagree and the
one that dies takes its whole top-level form with it (the #467 recovery load
then continues at the next form).

WHAT IT COSTS: t/comp/package.t `aborted-forms:1: The variable |$'b| is
unbound.`  The aborted form is the bare block at package.t:19-24, which does
nothing but assign, so the file still produces all 14 rows and this abort
costs ZERO rows on its own -- the file's 6 fail rows are the live-stash class
(not-supported.md §Live symbol-table hashes).  It is filed because it is a
LOUD abort with a known cause, and because a silent write to `|$main'a|`
instead of `$main::a` is the #138 family's shape in miniature.

FIX SHAPE: a token repair in the `_ppi_parse` pre-pass family (where the
`$Ｘ`/`%12`/`WORD /` repairs live) -- rewrite `'` to `::` inside a Symbol
token's NAME, with the leading-`'`-means-current-package rule, before the name
reaches `Pl::CLForm::cl_sym`.  PROBE THE CASE IT WOULD BREAK: `$'` alone is
POSTMATCH and must not become `$::`; `$'x` IS `$main::x` in perl even though
`$'` is a legal variable (perl's own tokenizer prefers the package reading
when an identifier follows), and a `'` inside a STRING must be untouched --
which is `Pl::InterpScan`'s escape/quote discipline, not the repair's.
subject: The OLD `'` package separator (`$main'a`, `$'b`) is read as part of the NAME, so `$'b` becomes the unbound global `|$'b|` and takes its whole top-level form -- t/comp/package.t's one aborted form
